content.title: About
content.content: Savoy cabbage is a variety of Brassica oleracea with crinkly, light‑green leaves. When cooked it retains a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a tender texture. It is commonly used in side dishes, soups, and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Savoy cabbage originates from the Mediterranean region but is now cultivated worldwide.
Its leaves have distinctive wavy margins that set it apart from regular green cabbage.
Savoy cabbage is a staple in many Eastern European dishes, such as Polish bigos.
Cooking preserves most of its B‑vitamins and vitamin C if not overcooked.
It is rich in antioxidants like quercetin.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked savoy cabbage provides a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber content promotes healthy bowel movements and feeds beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A serving of cooked savoy cabbage contains about 25 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytochemicals such as glucosinolates help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in cabbage contribute to normal blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Cabbage contains raffinose, which can cause gas and bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Thyroid interaction
items.content: Glucosinolates may affect thyroid function when consumed in large amounts raw; cooking reduces this risk.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to cabbage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked savoy cabbage can be served as a side dish, added to soups, stews, salads, or baked with cheese. It pairs well with carrots, onions, and spices such as caraway or dill.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked cabbage in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it (after cooling) in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months.
